title: Regularity after adjoining a coordinate
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $g:\\{−1,1\\}^n\\to\\{−1,1\\}$ be a sign-valued function. Suppose $g$ has mean zero and every nonempty Fourier coefficient of its real-valued sign representation has absolute value at most $\\varepsilon$, where $\\varepsilon\\ge 0$. Define a function on $\\{−1,1\\}^{n+1}$ by multiplying the first input coordinate by the value of $g$ on the remaining coordinates. Every nonempty Fourier coefficient of this function's real-valued sign representation then has absolute value at most $\\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: $g$ maps the sign cube to signs
the Fourier coefficients of the real-valued sign representation of $g$ are bounded by $\\varepsilon$ on every nonempty coordinate set
the mean of that real-valued representation is zero
